title: Turnaround Ops Audit and Save Canvas
body:
Purpose:
This is a working canvas for rapid account turnaround audits (15–48h) and a menu of targeted save plays for mid-risk renewals. Focus: create an auditable single-page summary that can be handed to an AM + Solutions engineer + Exec sponsor to align on next steps and an escalation path.

Intended use (quick):
- Run quick intake using the Rapid Audit Checklist below.
- Score account across 5 vectors to produce a one-line risk rating and recommended urgency.
- Choose 1 primary save play + 1 fallback; assign owners and 48h actions.
- Prep a one-paragraph executive escalation note if score >= 18.

Rapid Audit Checklist (do in a single call or internal sync; target 45–90 minutes):
- Customer profile: ARR, contract end date, renewal type (auto/manual), payment cadence, product footprint (routes, models in use).
- Recent telemetry: latency p50/p95, error spikes (>3x baseline), token spend drift, unusual 401/403 events.
- Product adoption signals: daily active routes, percent of routes with >0.1% errors, recent feature toggles.
- Business signals: expansion pipeline, churn signals from finance, executive contact frequency (last 90d).
- Support history: open P1/P2s, time-to-resolution last 90d, RCA status.
- Plan & expectations: promised deliverables from onboarding, outstanding tickets, backlog of feature requests that affect core flows.

5-Vector Risk Scoring (0–5 each; total 0–25):
- Technical Stability (0 none — 5 recurring outages causing business impact)
- Usage & Cost Drift (0 none — 5 runaway spend or sudden usage loss)
- Product Fit & Adoption (0 strong — 5 minimal adoption for paid features)
- Commercial & Contractual Pressure (0 healthy renewals — 5 executive signaled non-renewal)
- Support Experience & Escalations (0 great — 5 unresolved P0s with exec visibility)

Scoring guidance (examples):
- 20–25: High risk — immediate Exec escalation, dedicate Solutions/SE + SRE time, consider temporary credits or account freeze of non-critical routes.
- 13–19: Medium risk — prioritized action plan, focused technical remediation, PoC or sandbox for quick wins, CS director sync in 48h.
- 0–12: Low risk — monitor, normal renewal playbook.

Action Canvas (fill in one sheet per account):
- Account quick facts: {company, ARR, contract_end, renewal_type, AM},
- Score: total / 25 and vector breakdown,
- Prime hypothesis (single-sentence): why they might not renew,
- Primary save play (choose from menu), owner, 48h deliverables, success metrics (what reduces risk score),
- Fallback play, owner, timeline,
- Executive note needed? (Y/N) + draft snippet.

Save Plays Menu (pick 1 primary):
1) Rapid Reliability Intervention
   - Trigger: p95 latency regressions, token spike with service degradation.
   - Tactics: schedule emergency on-call SRE/serving-runtime war room for root cause; apply temporary routing to an older stable model variant; enable prefix caching for hot endpoints; create hot-fix rollout within 24h.
   - Commitment: 48h RCA + mitigation, daily updates to customer.
   - Signals to success: p95 back to SLA, no consumer incident reports for 72h.

2) Cost Containment & Usage Alignment
   - Trigger: >20% month-over-month spend increase or surprise overages.
   - Tactics: run cost-slicing report, apply soft quotas on high-volume routes, recommend quantized model variant for heavy batch workloads, schedule a cost-review call and share a 30/60/90 day cost plan.
   - Customer ask: agree to pilot quantized route for 2 weeks.

3) Feature-Fit Rapid PoC
   - Trigger: low adoption of key paid features driving value gap.
   - Tactics: 10-day focused PoC with product engineering + solutions lead; pre-built templates to integrate; success criteria defined up front (e.g., route adoption, latency, conversion uplift).
   - Commitment: demo at 10 days; if successful, include in renewal terms.

4) Executive Alignment & Contract Restructuring
   - Trigger: commercial tension or competitor threat.
   - Tactics: convene exec sponsor (AM + CS director + sales exec) for a 30–45m alignment call; offer targeted concessions (pilot credits, adjusted billing milestone) tied to adoption milestones; propose a short-term extension to lock revenue while fixes complete.
   - Safeguards: approvals matrix required for any discount.

5) White-Glove Migration Support
   - Trigger: customer expresses intent to move workloads or is pushing toward on-prem.
   - Tactics: offer migration runway plan, dedicated solutions engineering days bundled into short-term commitment, temporary data ingress/egress cost coverage, migration playbook with checkpoints.

Escalation Matrix (who to loop and when):
- AM + CS Lead (immediately after audit) — own customer comms.
- Solutions Engineering / SE on-call (same day) — technical remediation.
- SRE / Serving-runtime liaison (same day if technical instability) — perform mitigations.
- Director of CS (within 24h if score >=13) — resource prioritization.
- VP / CRO (within 48h if score >=18 OR exec threat reported) — negotiate commercial levers.

Exec Escalation Email Template (short, to be adapted):
Subject: Urgent: Renewal Risk — [Account] needs 48h stabilization
Hi [VP/CRO name],
Quick summary: [Account] (ARR $X) is at risk for renewal on [contract_end]. Rapid audit score = [score]/25 driven by [top 2 vectors]. Immediate impact: [impact paragraph: revenue, customer facing product down, competitor moving].
Requesting: 1) priority SE/SRE allocation for next 48h, 2) enable short-term commercial options (credits/extension) if technical fixes validated, 3) Exec alignment call within 48h.
Attachments: short canvas + timeline.
Thanks,
[AM] + [CS Lead]

Triage timeline (example for medium/high risk):
- Day 0 (audit day): complete canvas, assign owners, technical quick fixes started.
- Day 1: daily war room; customer sync; progress update to director.
- Day 2–3: implement primary play; measure signals; if failing, trigger fallback and exec call.
- Day 4–7: stabilize and document RCA; negotiate commercial if needed; prepare renewal plan.

Measurement & success criteria (examples):
- Technical: p95 latency reduced to baseline within 72h; error rate < baseline x1.2; no P0s for 7 days.
- Adoption: key route activation +10% week-over-week after PoC.
- Commercial: renewal committed or short-term extension with milestones.

Open questions / reminders (notes to self):
- Need quick access to customer billing snapshots in internal finance dashboard (ask Finance team).
- Confirm SRE on-call availability for weekend interventions (if contract_end < 10 days).
- Approvals process for emergency credits — who signs off under $X.
- Keep audit canvas exportable to Confluence and QBR slides (single slide summary).

Quick links to run during audit:
- Usage dashboard (internal): https://internal.redwood.ai/costs/[account_id]
- Incident timeline: https://stability.redwood.ai/incidents?customer=[account_id]
- Support ticket backlog: https://zendesk.redwood.ai/tickets?customer=[account_id]

Appendix: sample 48h check script for AM (script to follow with commands/prompts to run against dashboards; keep minimal)
1) Pull last 30 days token usage and filter by route.
2) Check p50/p95 for top 3 routes and compare to baseline.
3) Confirm any policy change toggles in last 14 days.
4) List open P1/P2 tickets and owners + ETA.
5) Prepare 3-slide summary for exec call: one-line problem, actions taken, ask.

Notes on format: this doc is a living canvas — prefer short bullets, links out to artifacts, and an explicit owner for each action. The goal is to turn ambiguous churn signals into measurable, actionable interventions that can be executed in 48–72 hours.

Last updated: 2026-03-01 by Aisha Patel (draft)
